content.comment_body: I have a program that counts pulses from a counter, and I want to create a line of code that allows modifying the setpoint directly, without requiring operator input on the [product_name] operator device.
This forum communicates in English. Please submit your posts in English.

Hello [user_name], Please use English when asking questions, as this community communicates in a single language for better support. Posting in English increases the chances of receiving answers to your question. Here is a translation of your issue. Best regards, [user_name]
Hello [user_name], Try activating the "Protection active" option in the block settings of your program, and then switch [product_name] to user mode after transferring the program.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is looking for a way to modify a setpoint directly within the [product_name] logic, bypassing operator adjustments on the hardware interface. Responses are primarily about forum language rules and a suggestion to enable protection features in the program settings, but do not provide a direct solution or confirmation that the user's objective—programmatically changing the setpoint—is achieved.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to update the setpoint through program logic, without manual input via the physical operator terminal.
